leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members explicitly prefer the optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) as a single-part prize. All five credit Katori with the magic-wavelength lattice idea and first strontium lattice clock, and Ye with taking uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and the many-body and spin-exchange physics. All five also reject waiting for the SI redefinition of the second. They differ in citation wording (Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth cite the 1e-18 level; Olsson adds precision tests; Pearce says a new regime of precision measurement) and in how much weight to put on prospective physics (constants, geodesy, dark matter) versus demonstrated results; Johansson and Olsson say the citation should rest on what has been shown. Their stated alternatives differ (B012/B049, B049/B056, B042/B059), so agreement on B008 is not agreement on a second choice. Kroll and Lindroth ranked it first in the opening ballots; Johansson, Olsson and Pearce each say they moved it to first place after reading the opening ballots, from circuit QED, aberration-corrected microscopy and IceCube respectively.

Two members explicitly prefer topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp). Both treat it as a new state of matter with a simple mechanism (Z2 invariant, helical edge states) and a decisive experiment, independently confirmed over about two decades. Both name the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (the HgTe proposal) and the separate 3D story as the main weakness, and Mehlig says he would rather lose the configuration than award it on a distorted record. They differ in how they would handle it: Eriksson argues that Kane and Mele's earlier Z2 and QSH concept plus Molenkamp's experiment is a complete core, and would treat 3D as a later item; Mehlig wants the citation worded around the concept and first observation, and notes that Kane and Mele's graphene mechanism is not the system where the effect was seen. Eriksson names B008 as fallback and Mehlig also lists B008 as an alternative.

One member explicitly prefers the Higgs discovery with ATLAS and CMS, with Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee. He argues the experimental half was left unrecognised in 2013, that the result is permanent, and that the trio spans both experiments. He concedes in his own case against that the three-of-four choice is a judgement the record cannot settle, and that he dropped Della Negra, whom he named in his opening ballot. Lindroth and Olsson list B056 as an alternative, and Johansson says he would support it if a defensible trio exists. Those are not explicit preferences in a configuration and are not counted as supporters.

areas_of_agreement: No member argues that the lattice clock, topological insulators or the Higgs discovery lacks scientific merit or maturity; the disagreement is mainly about attribution, category (invention versus discovery), and overlap with earlier prizes.

Five of eight members explicitly prefer B008 as a single-part configuration, and Eriksson and Mehlig, who prefer B049, each name B008 as a fallback or alternative. Danielsson also lists it as his first alternative.

Every member who addressed it (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce, Mehlig) says the pending SI redefinition of the second should not be a precondition for a physics prize. Eriksson asks whether it is better to wait, but this is not an expressed position.

Every member who addressed B049 or B056 identifies attribution, not science, as the main obstacle. For B049 it is the missing HgTe proposers and the separate 3D work; for B056 it is that any three of four ATLAS and CMS leaders drops a founder.
Several members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson) say they would be comfortable with B008 as the committee's outcome, even where it is not their first choice.

Members who prefer B008 agree the circuit QED candidate (B012) is not preferred this year, citing the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits and missing credit for Girvin and others; Johansson, its original advocate, moved to B008.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus invention: Danielsson and Eriksson argue that a new particle or a new state of matter is a stronger type of achievement than a measurement capability; Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce argue the lattice clock opens observables that were not accessible before.

Whether the lattice clock has yielded physics yet: Eriksson, Johansson and Pearce note that no deviation from standard physics has been found and that constants, geodesy and dark-matter reach are largely prospective, while Kroll and Lindroth cite the millimetre-scale redshift and many-body clock results as already demonstrated.

Whether Kane, Mele and Molenkamp's work forms a self-contained discovery. Eriksson says the QSH concept and Molenkamp's observation are a complete core; Mehlig, Johansson, Lindroth and Olsson say the HgTe experiment tested the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, not the Kane-Mele graphene model. Delicacy of the HgTe edge-transport evidence is also raised.

Whether topological insulators overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases. Mehlig and Eriksson list this; Johansson and Mehlig argue it concerns a different symmetry-class concept, and Eriksson treats it as unresolved.
Whether the 2013 theory prize already covers the Higgs discovery. Danielsson says it recognised the prediction, not the observation; this is not confirmed by the other members.

Whether electron optics (B009) is physics or a methods contribution; Olsson, who ranked it first on the opening ballot, does not include it in her preferred configuration, and Danielsson and Kroll question its fit with physics.
attribution_disputes: B008: Katori for the idea and first strontium lattice clock, Ye for performance and many-body physics. Kroll notes the invention could be argued as Katori's alone; Lemonde, Ludlow, Sterr, Gill and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups, and the ion-clock lineage, are outside the pair. Olsson and Lindroth ask whether any key systematic was established outside the two credited names, and no member has yet answered.

B008: proposed citations differ in emphasis (invention and development; 1e-18 level; precision tests; new regime of precision measurement), and Kroll and Pearce argue it must name both the invention and the development so that Ye's contribution is not lost.

B049: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) are outside the credited trio; Fu, Kane, Moore, Balents and Hasan (3D) are a separate story. Eriksson notes Zhang's death, which Mehlig and others do not mention, and a 2D-only citation cannot cover 3D within a three-person limit.

B056: round-1 and opening proposals name different trios from the same four credited people: Danielsson (round 1), Lindroth and Pearce chose Gianotti, Jenni, Virdee, while Olsson's opening trio was Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni. Olsson and Pearce question whether spokesperson titles map reliably onto original work, and Pearce says he has no principled rule.
B012 (not preferred by any member in round 1): Johansson notes that Girvin and Huard are outside the credited trio, which Kroll and Lindroth also cite.
maturity_disputes: B008: independently reproduced and surpassed in several laboratories (Sr, Yb, Hg) with routine international comparisons; no member disputes maturity. The pending SI redefinition is raised as a question but five members reject it as a precondition.
B049: all members regard it as mature (about two decades, several material families), but Mehlig and Johansson say the edge-transport evidence in HgTe is more delicate than the topology concept.
B056: not disputed as mature; Danielsson cites a decade of coupling measurements.

B042 (IceCube, my own opening first choice, now an alternative): the existence of the diffuse astrophysical flux is secure, but source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are at moderate significance and most of the flux is unidentified. Danielsson, Kroll and Olsson cite this as a maturity limit.
B035 (twisted bilayer graphene): Danielsson says the pairing mechanism is unresolved, which he finds hard to square with the usual maturity requirement.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll: a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his PhD, with Ye associated with the Hall/JILA group, and he says the committee may wish to consider recusal on B008. He also has leadership at WACQT, whose superconducting-qubit work relies on B012. He says there is no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye.

Johansson: directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, works with superconducting-circuit groups, and says he should recuse from B012 and avoid pressing it. He reports no apparent tie to B008.

Olsson: field-proximity conflict with B009 as an electron microscopist and IFSM President, and she proposes to recuse from deciding that candidate. She asks Johansson to state whether he will recuse on B012.

Lindroth: close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and the Lund and Keller attosecond groups, and a close reader of the lattice-clock field; she sees no recusal requirement for B008 but notes field proximity.

Pearce (Chair): member of PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur; Fermi-LAT overlaps with the wider multi-messenger follow-up of TXS 0506+056, a field-proximity tie to B042, which is only an alternative. No tie to Katori or Ye is apparent.
Mehlig: same Gothenburg physics environment as Johansson and Olsson, with no specific collaboration and no recusal proposed.
Danielsson and Eriksson: no specific conflict apparent for any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: B008: if five members prefer the lattice clock, can the committee agree on a citation that names the magic-wavelength lattice invention and its realisation at 1e-18, and that rests only on demonstrated results, so as to answer the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control overlap objection?

B008: was any key systematic (lattice light shift, blackbody radiation, hyperpolarisability, density shift) established by a group outside Katori and Ye, and does that change the credit boundary against SYRTE, PTB, NIST, Lemonde, Ludlow, Sterr and the ion-clock lineage? Lindroth is best placed to answer.
B008: given Kroll's disclosed ties to the Hall/JILA group, how should the committee handle his participation in the final ballot on B008 (recusal, or participation with the disclosure noted)?

B049 versus B008: can Eriksson and Mehlig show that Kane, Mele and Molenkamp stand as a complete discovery without the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, and can they agree on a citation that does not misstate the lineage? Is the 2016 overlap a real objection?

B056: is there a principled rule for choosing three of Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee (for example spokespersons at discovery), and would Danielsson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each accept it? If not, is the Higgs a prize this committee can award under the three-person limit?

Category: should the committee prefer a discovery about nature or a new measurement capability when attribution is cleaner for the latter, and does it matter that no deviation from standard physics has yet been found with lattice clocks?

Combined configurations: Kroll raises a two-part prize that pairs B008 with another part, but the three-person cap makes a split awkward. Does any member want to propose such a configuration in round 2, and which parts and names?
Fallbacks: should B012, B042, B059 and B009 remain open as alternatives in the final ballot, given Johansson's and Olsson's proposed recusals and the 2025 circuits prize?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a plurality for the optical lattice clock, with five of eight explicit preferences, two for topological insulators and one for the Higgs discovery. Scientific merit and maturity are not seriously contested for any of the three. The substantive disagreements concern attribution (the missing HgTe proposers, the choice of three from four ATLAS and CMS founders, and the boundary around Katori and Ye), overlap with earlier prizes, and whether a measurement capability weighs as much as a discovery. The five supporters of B008 include the Chair, who moved to it from his opening first choice, and this count is a description of round 1, not a decision. I have counted only positions explicit in the eight round-1 files, and round 2 should test the objections to B008 and the attribution questions for B049 and B056 before any final ballot.
